I will still start from what I did before, because with only 4.1 mu I cannot afford to gamble. On my land in Quzhou, wheat and maize are the main stomach crops, so I will keep most of the ground in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I finished middle school, so I do look at cost and yield together, not just follow habit. If fertilizer is too short, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a little extra on one more bag. So this year I will put the steadier land into 3.1 mu of wheat followed by summer maize, and I will keep 1.0 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen around jointing. With well water, I will irrigate about three times if the season is normal. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, plant as soon as wheat comes off, and push nitrogen a bit because summer maize responds quickly if rain and water are there. For cotton, I will not make the area big because it takes more watching and spraying, and my household labor is limited. I will still feed cotton enough potassium, because if bolls set well but fertilizer is weak, the plant goes empty. I will follow what has worked around me: not the lowest input, not the fanciest input, just a solid plan that protects yield and fits my money and labor.
